body.en: In every collision the total linear momentum is conserved. In an *elastic* collision the total kinetic energy is also conserved. In an inelastic collision some kinetic energy turns into heat, sound or deformation. In a completely inelastic collision the bodies stick together and move with a common velocity $v = \dfrac{m_1u_1 + m_2u_2}{m_1 + m_2}$.
body.kn: ಪ್ರತಿಯೊಂದು ಸಂಘಟ್ಟನೆಯಲ್ಲೂ ಒಟ್ಟು ರೇಖೀಯ ಸಂವೇಗ ಸಂರಕ್ಷಿತ. ಸ್ಥಿತಿಸ್ಥಾಪಕ ಸಂಘಟ್ಟನೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಚಲನ ಶಕ್ತಿಯೂ ಸಂರಕ್ಷಿತ. ಅಸ್ಥಿತಿಸ್ಥಾಪಕ ಸಂಘಟ್ಟನೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ ಚಲನ ಶಕ್ತಿ ಉಷ್ಣ, ಶಬ್ದ ಅಥವಾ ವಿರೂಪಣೆಯಾಗಿ ಬದಲಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಸಂಪೂರ್ಣ ಅಸ್ಥಿತಿಸ್ಥಾಪಕ ಸಂಘಟ್ಟನೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಕಾಯಗಳು ಅಂಟಿಕೊಳ್ಳುತ್ತವೆ.

Completely inelastic: maximum loss of KE.
Ball one, mass m one, hits ball two at rest. After the collision both may move.
Momentum is conserved in every collision, and in an elastic one kinetic energy is too. Solving both gives the final velocities.
Equal masses simply exchange velocities. A light ball hitting a very heavy one bounces straight back.
If the bodies stick together, the collision is completely inelastic and kinetic energy is always lost.

narration.en: In every collision the total momentum is the same before and after. In an elastic collision kinetic energy is also conserved; in an inelastic one some is lost; in a perfectly inelastic one the carts stick together and the most energy is lost. The coefficient of restitution e = (v₂ − v₁)/(u₁ − u₂) tells which.

body.en: If m₁ moving at u₁ hits m₂ at rest head-on and elastically, $v_1 = \dfrac{(m_1 - m_2)u_1}{m_1 + m_2}$ and $v_2 = \dfrac{2m_1u_1}{m_1 + m_2}$. Equal masses exchange velocities. A light body bouncing off a very heavy one simply reverses its velocity. In two *dimensions*, momentum is conserved separately along x and along y.
body.kn: m₁ ದ್ರವ್ಯರಾಶಿ u₁ ವೇಗದಲ್ಲಿ ನಿಶ್ಚಲ m₂ ಗೆ ನೇರವಾಗಿ ಸ್ಥಿತಿಸ್ಥಾಪಕವಾಗಿ ಬಡಿದರೆ v₁ = (m₁ − m₂)u₁/(m₁ + m₂), v₂ = 2m₁u₁/(m₁ + m₂). ಸಮ ದ್ರವ್ಯರಾಶಿಗಳು ವೇಗಗಳನ್ನು ವಿನಿಮಯ ಮಾಡಿಕೊಳ್ಳುತ್ತವೆ.

points.en: Two *dimensions*: conserve pₓ and pᵧ separately

narration.en: If m₁ moving at u₁ hits m₂ at rest head-on and elastically, $v_1 = \dfrac{(m_1 - m_2)u_1}{m_1 + m_2}$ and $v_2 = \dfrac{2m_1u_1}{m_1 + m_2}$. Equal masses exchange velocities. A light body bouncing off a very heavy one simply reverses its velocity. In two dimensions, momentum is conserved separately along x and along y.
narration.kn: m₁ ದ್ರವ್ಯರಾಶಿ u₁ ವೇಗದಲ್ಲಿ ನಿಶ್ಚಲ m₂ ಗೆ ನೇರವಾಗಿ ಸ್ಥಿತಿಸ್ಥಾಪಕವಾಗಿ ಬಡಿದರೆ v₁ = (m₁ − m₂)u₁/(m₁ + m₂), v₂ = 2m₁u₁/(m₁ + m₂). ಸಮ ದ್ರವ್ಯರಾಶಿಗಳು ವೇಗಗಳನ್ನು ವಿನಿಮಯ ಮಾಡಿಕೊಳ್ಳುತ್ತವೆ.

say.en: If m 1 moving at u 1 hits m 2 at rest head-on and elastically, v 1 equals (m 1 minus m 2u 1) over m 1 plus m 2 and v 2 equals 2 metres 1u 1 over m 1 plus m 2. Equal masses exchange velocities. A light body bouncing off a very heavy one simply reverses its velocity. In two dimensions, momentum is conserved separately along x and along y. Equal masses: velocities are exchanged.
say.kn: m 1 ದ್ರವ್ಯರಾಶಿ u 1 ವೇಗದಲ್ಲಿ ನಿಶ್ಚಲ m 2 ಗೆ ನೇರವಾಗಿ ಸ್ಥಿತಿಸ್ಥಾಪಕವಾಗಿ ಬಡಿದರೆ v 1 equals (m 1 - m 2)u 1 over m 1 plus m 2, v 2 equals 2m 1u 1 over m 1 plus m 2. ಸಮ ದ್ರವ್ಯರಾಶಿಗಳು ವೇಗಗಳನ್ನು ವಿನಿಮಯ ಮಾಡಿಕೊಳ್ಳುತ್ತವೆ.

myth.en: In an inelastic collision some momentum is lost, just like some kinetic energy.

truth.en: Momentum is conserved in every collision, elastic or not. Only kinetic energy can be lost (into heat, sound and deformation). Momentum and kinetic energy both depend on mass and speed, so it feels as if they should behave alike. But momentum is a vector changed only by external forces, while kinetic energy can be converted into other forms by internal forces.

say.en: Momentum is conserved in every collision; kinetic energy only in elastic ones.
Completely inelastic: $v_f = m_1v_{1i}/(m_1 + m_2)$; KE loss $= \tfrac12\,\tfrac{m_1m_2}{m_1 + m_2}\,v_{1i}^2$.
Elastic, $m_2$ at rest: $v_{1f} = \tfrac{m_1 - m_2}{m_1 + m_2}v_{1i}$, $v_{2f} = \tfrac{2m_1}{m_1 + m_2}v_{1i}$.
Equal masses in an elastic head-on collision exchange velocities.
In 2D, conserve each momentum component; equal masses, elastic, one at rest: they separate at 90°.

question.en: In a reactor, fast neutrons are best slowed down by elastic collisions with nuclei that are:

options.en: light, with mass close to the neutron's
of any mass; it makes no difference

explain.en: Equal masses exchange velocities, so a neutron hitting a light nucleus head-on hands over most of its energy. A heavy nucleus would just bounce it back with almost the same speed.

task.en: Equal balls, elastic head-on hit, B at rest. Afterwards?

question.en: Equal balls, elastic head-on hit, B at rest. Afterwards?

options.en: A stops and B moves off with A's speed
A and B both move forward at half of A's speed
A bounces back and B stays at rest

explain.en: With equal masses the elastic result gives v₁f = 0 and v₂f = v₁i: they exchange velocities. Moving together at half speed is the completely inelastic case, which loses half the kinetic energy.

takeaway.en: Momentum is conserved in every collision; kinetic energy only in elastic ones.

problem.en: A 2 kg ball moving at 6 m/s collides with and sticks to a 1 kg ball at rest. Find their common velocity and the loss of kinetic energy.

steps.en: KE before = ½ × 2 × 36 = 36 J; KE after = ½ × 3 × 16 = 24 J.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A 2 kg ball moving at 6 m/s collides with and sticks to a 1 kg ball at rest. Find their common velocity and the loss of kinetic energy.

say.en: Let us solve this together. A 2 kilograms ball moving at 6 metres per second collides with and sticks to a 1 kilogram ball at rest. Find their common velocity and the loss of kinetic energy.
Momentum: 2 times 6 equals 3 times v, so v equals 4 metres per second.
KE before equals one half times 2 times 36 equals 36 joules; KE after equals one half times 3 times 16 equals 24 joules.
Loss of KE equals 12 joules.
So the answer is 4 metres per second; 12 joules lost.

problem.en: A 1 kg ball moving at 4 m/s makes a head-on elastic collision with a 3 kg ball at rest. Find their velocities after the collision.

steps.en: Check KE: 8 J before; ½(1)(4) + ½(3)(4) = 2 + 6 = 8 J after.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A 1 kg ball moving at 4 m/s makes a head-on elastic collision with a 3 kg ball at rest. Find their velocities after the collision.

say.en: Let us solve this together. A 1 kilogram ball moving at 4 metres per second makes a head-on elastic collision with a 3 kilograms ball at rest. Find their velocities after the collision.
v 1 equals 1 minus 3 times 4 divided by 4 equals minus 2 metres per second it bounces back.
v 2 equals 2 times 1 times 4 divided by 4 equals 2 metres per second.
Check KE: 8 joules before; one half 14 plus one half 34 equals 2 plus 6 equals 8 joules after.
So the answer is minus 2 metres per second and 2 metres per second.

heading.en: They leave as fast as they met

body.en: In a one-dimensional elastic collision, the speed of separation equals the speed of approach: v₂ − v₁ = u₁ − u₂. Use this with momentum conservation instead of the kinetic energy equation and you avoid the squares.

say.en: Pause and solve this exam pattern question. A ball of mass m moving at speed u collides with an identical ball at rest and they stick together. The fraction of the kinetic energy lost is.
Common velocity u over 2.
KE after equals one half 2 metres(u over 2) squared equals mu squared/4, half of mu squared/2.
So half the KE is lost.
